verifications.claim: The World Trade Organization (WTO) is the only global international organization managing rules of trade between nations.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "In brief, the World Trade Organization (WTO) is the only international organization dealing with the global rules of trade."
verifications.reasoning: R5 directly states WTO is the only international organization dealing with global rules of trade, matching the claim precisely.

verifications.claim: WTO was established in 1995.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "established in 1995"; R2: "Established: 1 January 1995"; R5: "The World Trade Organization came into being in 1995."
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references directly confirm establishment in 1995.

verifications.claim: WTO serves 166 members.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "today includes 166 members"; R2: "The WTO has 166 members"; R5: "The WTO has 166 members"
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of 166 members in multiple current sources.

verifications.claim: WTO members account for 98% of world trade.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: "accounting for 98% of world trade"; R5: "166 members, accounting for 98% of world trade."
verifications.reasoning: Exact figure directly stated in references.

verifications.claim: WTO negotiates agreements.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "serving as a negotiating forum for trade liberalization and rules"; R2: "Forum for trade negotiations"; R5: "acting as a forum for trade negotiations"
verifications.reasoning: Direct statements confirm WTO's role in negotiating agreements.

verifications.claim: WTO settles disputes.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "providing a dispute settlement (DS) process to resolve disputes"; R2: "Handling trade disputes"
verifications.reasoning: Explicit mention of dispute settlement function.

verifications.claim: WTO monitors trade policies.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: "Monitoring national trade policies"; R5: "reviewing members' trade policies"
verifications.reasoning: Direct references to monitoring and reviewing trade policies.

verifications.claim: WTO sets rules for international commerce in goods.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "WTO agreements cover trade in goods"; R5: "Goods ... the GATT spelt out important rules"
verifications.reasoning: WTO agreements explicitly cover rules for trade in goods.

verifications.claim: WTO sets rules for international commerce in services.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "trade in goods, agriculture and services"; R5: "Services ... General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS)"
verifications.reasoning: Direct coverage of services in WTO agreements.

verifications.claim: WTO sets rules for international commerce in intellectual property.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "intellectual property rights (IPR)"; R5: "Intellectual property The WTO’s Intellectual Property Agreement"
verifications.reasoning: Explicit rules for intellectual property via TRIPS.

verifications.claim: WTO provides a system to resolve trade conflicts between member countries.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "providing a dispute settlement (DS) process to resolve disputes"; R5: "Dispute settlement The WTO’s procedure for resolving trade conflicts"
verifications.reasoning: Dispute settlement system directly supports this.

verifications.claim: WTO reviews national trade policies.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The WTO's Trade Policy Review Mechanism is designed to improve transparency ... reviewing members' trade policies"
verifications.reasoning: Trade Policy Review Mechanism explicitly reviews policies.

verifications.claim: WTO ensures transparency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "transparency"; R6: "make countries’ trade rules as clear and public (transparent)"; R7: "Predictability and transparency"
verifications.reasoning: Core principle and mechanisms ensure transparency.

verifications.claim: WTO assists developing economies to participate in the global trading system.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: "provide technical assistance to developing countries"; R5: "building the trade capacity of developing economies"
verifications.reasoning: Technical assistance and capacity building directly stated.

verifications.claim: WTO rules are based on agreements signed by member countries and ratified in their parliaments.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: "they are ratified by members’ parliaments"; R9: "ratified in their legislatures"
verifications.reasoning: Agreements require ratification in parliaments/legislatures.

verifications.claim: WTO's most-favoured-nation principle involves treating all members equally.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: "Most-favoured-nation (MFN): treating other people equally"
verifications.reasoning: MFN principle explicitly described as treating equally.

verifications.claim: WTO's national treatment principle involves treating foreigners and locals equally.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "National treatment: Treating foreigners and locals equally"
verifications.reasoning: Exact description in R6.

verifications.claim: WTO requires members to disclose trade regulations.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Many WTO agreements require governments to disclose their policies and practices publicly"
verifications.reasoning: Direct requirement for disclosure.

verifications.claim: WTO allows flexibility for environmental protection.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: "protect ... the environment"; R7: "The WTO agreements permit members to take measures to protect ... the environment."
verifications.reasoning: Exceptions allowed for environmental protection.

verifications.claim: WTO allows flexibility for national security.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "WTO rules permit flexibility for governments to impose temporary measures justified by national security"
verifications.reasoning: Explicit flexibility for national security.

verifications.claim: WTO allows flexibility for developing country needs.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: "preferential treatment/flexibilities for developing countries"; R5: "gives developing economies some flexibility"
verifications.reasoning: Special flexibilities for developing countries confirmed.

verifications.claim: WTO decisions are made by member governments through consensus.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: "Decisions are normally taken by consensus"; R5: "typically by consensus"
verifications.reasoning: Consensus is the standard process for decisions.

verifications.claim: WTO Ministerial Conference occurs every two years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: "which meets usually every two years"; R5: "which meets usually every two years"
verifications.reasoning: Biennial meetings directly stated.

verifications.claim: WTO General Council is in Geneva.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "the General Council, which meets several times a year in Geneva."
verifications.reasoning: Location explicitly in Geneva.

verifications.claim: All WTO decisions are adopted by consensus of all members.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: "Decisions are normally taken by consensus"; R5: "typically by consensus"; R9: "foresees votes where consensus cannot be reached"
verifications.reasoning: References indicate consensus is normal/typical but not for all decisions; voting is possible.

verifications.claim: WTO Secretariat is located in Geneva, Switzerland.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: "Location: Geneva, Switzerland"; R5: "based in Geneva"
verifications.reasoning: Direct location confirmation.

verifications.claim: WTO Secretariat provides administrative support.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: "support the WTO's various councils and committees"; R5: "supply technical support for the various councils/ committees"
verifications.reasoning: Main duties include administrative and technical support.

verifications.claim: WTO Secretariat is currently led by Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: "Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is the seventh Director-General"; R5: "DIRECTOR GENERAL: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala"
verifications.reasoning: Current Director-General explicitly named.
